questions.prompt: The main verb; the main action that the subject is doing
questions.explanation: "The main verb" = just the one key action word.

questions.prompt: All the words that show together what the subject is doing
questions.explanation: "All the words" about what the subject is doing = the whole predicate.

questions.prompt: The main person, place, or thing doing the action in a sentence
questions.explanation: The one key noun of the subject.

questions.prompt: When the subject is doing more than one action in a sentence
questions.explanation: More than one action = more than one verb.

questions.prompt: All the words that state and describe the subject
questions.explanation: "All the words" that name and describe the subject.

questions.prompt: When there is more than one subject in a sentence
questions.explanation: More than one subject = compound subject.

questions.prompt: Brutus
questions.explanation: One noun with no describing words.

questions.prompt: Brutus Buckeye, Ohio State's mascot, ...
questions.explanation: Brutus Buckeye plus the renaming phrase Ohio State's mascot.

questions.prompt: Brutus Buckeye and the Jedi Knights
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by and.

questions.prompt: is
questions.explanation: A single verb.

questions.prompt: is running to the store
questions.explanation: The verb is running plus to the store. (is running alone = simple predicate)

questions.prompt: went to the store and bought an Xbox
questions.explanation: Two actions, went and bought, joined by and.

questions.prompt: [[Mrs. Harding and Ms. Garcia]] drink different flavors of tea.
questions.explanation: Two people joined by and.

questions.prompt: Mrs. Harding and Ms. Garcia [[drink]] different flavors of tea.
questions.explanation: Only the single verb drink.

questions.prompt: Mrs. Harding and Ms. Garcia [[drink different flavors of tea]].
questions.explanation: The verb plus everything after it. Only one verb, so not compound.

questions.prompt: Although it was late at night, [[we]] still went to the movie premiere.
questions.explanation: The main part is we still went... The word it belongs to the extra (dependent) part.

questions.prompt: [[The student]] did well on the grammar test.
questions.explanation: The + student = complete subject. (student alone = simple subject)

questions.prompt: The student [[studied hard and succeeded on the test]].
questions.explanation: Two actions, studied and succeeded, joined by and.

questions.prompt: The tall [[giraffe]] ate leaves from the tree.
questions.explanation: Giraffe is the one key noun.

questions.prompt: [[The tall giraffe]] ate leaves from the tree.
questions.explanation: The key noun plus The tall.

questions.prompt: [[My brother and my cousin]] played soccer after school.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by and.

questions.prompt: The puppy [[barked]] loudly at the mail carrier.
questions.explanation: Only the main verb barked.

questions.prompt: The puppy [[barked loudly at the mail carrier]].
questions.explanation: The verb plus everything after it.

questions.prompt: Grandma [[baked cookies and packed them in a box]].
questions.explanation: Two actions: baked and packed.

questions.prompt: After the storm ended, the [[children]] ran outside.
questions.explanation: The main part is the children ran outside.

questions.prompt: [[Lions, tigers, and bears]] live at the zoo.
questions.explanation: Three subjects joined by commas and and.

questions.prompt: Running down the hallway.
questions.explanation: No subject and no complete verb. Fix: Maya was running down the hallway.

questions.prompt: The red bicycle in the garage.
questions.explanation: No predicate. Fix: The red bicycle in the garage has a flat tire.

questions.prompt: [[The hungry bear]] searched for honey.
questions.explanation: The key noun bear plus its describing words The hungry = complete subject.

questions.prompt: My aunt [[sings and dances in the talent show]].
questions.explanation: One subject (my aunt) doing two actions: sings and dances.

questions.prompt: The [[bus]] stopped at the corner.
questions.explanation: Only the one key noun bus is underlined. The is not included.

questions.prompt: [[Pizza and tacos]] are my favorite foods.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by and.

questions.prompt: The kids [[laughed]] at the funny movie.
questions.explanation: Only the main verb laughed is underlined.

questions.prompt: Our teacher [[read a story to the class]].
questions.explanation: The verb read plus everything after it. Only one verb, so it is not compound.

questions.prompt: [[Dad and I]] washed the car on Saturday.
questions.explanation: Two subjects, Dad and I, joined by and.

questions.prompt: Because it was raining, [[we]] played board games inside.
questions.explanation: The main part is we played board games inside. "Because it was raining" is an extra (dependent) part, so it is not the main subject.

questions.prompt: Jumped over the fence.
questions.explanation: There is no subject. Who jumped? Fix: The dog jumped over the fence.

questions.prompt: The bell rang.
questions.explanation: It is short, but it has a subject (The bell) and a predicate (rang). That makes it complete.

questions.prompt: The students [[cleaned the classroom and packed their bags]].
questions.explanation: Two actions, cleaned and packed, joined by and.

questions.prompt: [[Several small birds]] sat on the wire.
questions.explanation: The key noun birds plus Several small = complete subject.

questions.prompt: The baby [[smiled at her mother]].
questions.explanation: The verb smiled plus the words after it. One verb only.

questions.prompt: My [[friend]] lives across the street.
questions.explanation: Only the key noun friend is underlined. My is a describing word.

questions.prompt: [[Tom, Lisa, and Kenji]] joined the art club.
questions.explanation: Three subjects joined with commas and and.

questions.prompt: The chef [[chopped]] the onions quickly.
questions.explanation: Only the main verb chopped is underlined.

questions.prompt: [[The old wooden bridge]] creaked in the wind.
questions.explanation: The key noun bridge plus The old wooden = complete subject.

questions.prompt: The cat [[stretched, yawned, and fell asleep]].
questions.explanation: Three actions: stretched, yawned, fell. More than one = compound predicate.

questions.prompt: She smiled.
questions.explanation: It has a subject (She) and a predicate (smiled). Short sentences can still be complete.

questions.prompt: My best friend from Texas.
questions.explanation: There is a subject but no predicate. What did the friend do? Fix: My best friend from Texas visited me.

questions.prompt: When the movie ended, the [[audience]] clapped.
questions.explanation: The main part is the audience clapped. "When the movie ended" is an extra (dependent) part, so movie is not the main subject.

questions.prompt: The runners [[crossed the finish line]].
questions.explanation: The verb crossed plus everything after it.

questions.prompt: [[Apples or bananas]] make a healthy snack.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by or. Compound subjects can use or as well as and.

questions.prompt: Mom [[locked the door and turned off the lights]].
questions.explanation: Two actions, locked and turned, joined by and.

questions.prompt: The team [[won]] the championship.
questions.explanation: Only the main verb won is underlined.

questions.prompt: [[My little brother's soccer coach]] blew the whistle.
questions.explanation: The key noun is coach. All the words before it describe him, so this is the complete subject.

questions.prompt: The dog [[was sleeping]] under the table.
questions.explanation: was sleeping is a helping verb + main verb. Together they count as ONE verb, so it is the simple predicate.

questions.prompt: The wind [[howled and shook the windows]].
questions.explanation: Two actions, howled and shook, joined by and.

questions.prompt: Birds sing.
questions.explanation: Only two words, but it has a subject (Birds) and a predicate (sing).

questions.prompt: Under the big oak tree.
questions.explanation: It has no subject and no verb. It only tells a place. Fix: We ate lunch under the big oak tree.

questions.prompt: The tall [[girl]] with red shoes won the race.
questions.explanation: Only the word girl is underlined. It is the one main word that tells who won the race, so it is the simple subject.

questions.prompt: [[The tall girl with red shoes]] won the race.
questions.explanation: The underlined part is the main word girl plus all the words that describe her (The tall ... with red shoes), so it is the complete subject.

questions.prompt: The baby [[laughed]] at the funny puppy.
questions.explanation: Only the verb laughed is underlined, so it is the simple predicate.

questions.prompt: The baby [[laughed at the funny puppy]].
questions.explanation: The underlined part is the verb laughed plus all the words after it, so it is the complete predicate.

questions.prompt: Our teacher [[smiled and waved at the class]].
questions.explanation: The teacher does two actions, smiled and waved, joined by and, so it is a compound predicate.

questions.prompt: After the game ended, [[we]] ate pizza together.
questions.explanation: We is one word, and it tells who ate the pizza, so it is the simple subject. Be careful: "After the game ended" is extra information at the beginning. It is not the subject of the sentence.

questions.prompt: [[Cats, dogs, and rabbits]] live at the animal shelter.
questions.explanation: There are three subjects (cats, dogs, rabbits) doing the same action, so it is a compound subject. A compound subject can have more than two parts!

questions.prompt: The old wooden bridge [[creaked]] in the strong wind.
questions.explanation: Only the verb creaked is underlined, so it is the simple predicate. Tip: "old" and "wooden" are describing words, not verbs.

questions.prompt: The students [[cleaned the classroom and went home]].
questions.explanation: The students do two actions, cleaned and went, so it is a compound predicate.

questions.prompt: [[My grandmother]] bakes bread every Sunday.
questions.explanation: The underlined part is the main word grandmother plus the describing word My, so it is the complete subject.

questions.prompt: The children [[sang and danced at the festival]].
questions.explanation: The children do two actions, sang and danced, joined by and, so it is a compound predicate.

questions.prompt: The small gray [[kitten]] slept on the sofa.
questions.explanation: Only kitten is underlined. It is the one main word that tells who slept, so it is the simple subject.

questions.prompt: [[Tom and Lisa]] walked to the library.
questions.explanation: There are two people, joined by and, doing the same action, so it is a compound subject.

questions.prompt: The bus [[arrived]] late this morning.
questions.explanation: Only the verb arrived is underlined, so it is the simple predicate.

questions.prompt: The bus [[arrived late this morning]].
questions.explanation: The underlined part is the verb arrived plus all the words after it, so it is the complete predicate.

questions.prompt: [[The best player on our team]] scored two goals.
questions.explanation: The main word is player. The underlined part includes all the words that describe the player, so it is the complete subject.

questions.prompt: Before school started, [[Kenji]] finished his homework.
questions.explanation: Kenji is one word, and he is the one who finished the homework, so it is the simple subject. "Before school started" is extra information.

questions.prompt: My dad [[washed the car and cut the grass]].
questions.explanation: My dad does two actions, washed and cut, so it is a compound predicate.

questions.prompt: [[Apples and bananas]] are my favorite fruits.
questions.explanation: There are two subjects, apples and bananas, joined by and, so it is a compound subject.

questions.prompt: The hungry lion [[roared]] at the crowd.
questions.explanation: Only the verb roared is underlined, so it is the simple predicate.

questions.prompt: [[Sara, Mike, and Ben]] joined the art club.
questions.explanation: There are three people doing the same action, so it is a compound subject.

questions.prompt: [[The girl in the blue jacket]] is my best friend.
questions.explanation: The main word is girl. The underlined part includes all the words that describe her, so it is the complete subject.

questions.prompt: The birds [[flew over the lake]].
questions.explanation: The underlined part is the verb flew plus all the words after it, so it is the complete predicate.

questions.prompt: My little [[sister]] loves chocolate ice cream.
questions.explanation: Only sister is underlined. It is the one main word, so it is the simple subject.

questions.prompt: The chef [[chopped the onions and stirred the soup]].
questions.explanation: The chef does two actions, chopped and stirred, so it is a compound predicate.

questions.prompt: During the storm, [[the lights]] went out.
questions.explanation: The underlined part is the main word lights plus the, so it is the complete subject. "During the storm" is extra information, not the subject.

questions.prompt: The students [[listened carefully to the speaker]].
questions.explanation: The underlined part is the verb listened plus all the words after it, so it is the complete predicate.

questions.prompt: [[Rain and wind]] hit the small town.
questions.explanation: There are two subjects, rain and wind, joined by and, so it is a compound subject.

questions.prompt: Our class [[visited]] the science museum.
questions.explanation: Only the verb visited is underlined, so it is the simple predicate.

questions.prompt: The friendly [[dog]] wagged its tail.
questions.explanation: Only dog is underlined. It is the one main word that tells who wagged its tail, so it is the simple subject.

questions.prompt: My mom [[read the letter and smiled]].
questions.explanation: My mom does two actions, read and smiled, so it is a compound predicate.

questions.prompt: [[The new students from Canada]] joined our class.
questions.explanation: The main word is students. The underlined part includes all the words that describe them, so it is the complete subject.

questions.prompt: The sun [[rises in the east]].
questions.explanation: The underlined part is the verb rises plus all the words after it, so it is the complete predicate.

questions.prompt: [[Pencils and erasers]] are on sale today.
questions.explanation: There are two subjects, pencils and erasers, joined by and, so it is a compound subject.

questions.prompt: The movie [[ended]] at nine o'clock.
questions.explanation: Only the verb ended is underlined, so it is the simple predicate.

questions.prompt: When the bell rang, [[everyone]] ran outside.
questions.explanation: Everyone is one word, and it tells who ran outside, so it is the simple subject. "When the bell rang" is extra information.

questions.prompt: The team [[practiced hard and won the championship]].
questions.explanation: The team does two actions, practiced and won, so it is a compound predicate.

questions.prompt: [[My uncle and his dog]] went fishing.
questions.explanation: There are two subjects, my uncle and his dog, joined by and, so it is a compound subject.

questions.prompt: The flowers in the garden [[bloomed beautifully]].
questions.explanation: The underlined part is the verb bloomed plus the word after it, so it is the complete predicate.
